summary: Europe is fighting an energy shock from the Iran war. Euro area inflation was 3.2% in August, with energy up 14.3% from a year ago, and markets expect the ECB to keep raising rates from a deposit rate of about 2.50% (next decision Oct 29). The brief Russia Ukraine 'energy ceasefire' has failed: Zelenskyy said Ukraine will resume strikes on Russian refineries, and Russia reported a hit on the Ryazan refinery on Oct 15, which keeps diesel tight into winter. ASML beat and raised on Oct 14. High energy hurts chemicals and industry, while oil majors and banks gain. Reuters reported on Oct 17 that the Ryazan refinery's main crude unit is still halted after the Oct 15 strike, and a drone set fire to Russia's Surgut condensate plant on Oct 16. On Oct 19 riots in France pushed its 10 year yield toward 4.9% and hit French banks, with a Moody's review due Oct 23. The US waived new Russia oil tariffs on Oct 16, easing oil but angering Kyiv. France did not vote on its budget on Oct 20: the National Assembly set the revenue vote for Nov 3, so Moody's (Aa3, negative outlook) reviews France on Oct 23 with no budget decision. The prime minister promised more curfews, and the CAC 40 fell 0.38% to 7,838.49 on Oct 20. On Oct 21 France's 10 year yield touched 5%, its highest since 2002, and it reached about 5.10% on Oct 22, with the gap over Germany near its widest since 2011, a day before Moody's review.
for_you: Europe is fighting energy driven inflation and now French fiscal stress. More ECB hikes are likely (Oct 29). European bank ADRs (SAN, ING) gain from higher rates but are hurt by the French selloff, so wait until after Moody's on Oct 23. ASML is the one European name that matters for your AI themes.

changes.what: The Stoxx 600 gained about 1% and erased its weekly loss as Brent and euro bond yields eased after Trump said the US would not attack Iran before the midterms. Carmakers rose on progress in EU-China trade talks.

The Stoxx 600 rose to about 635 on Monday morning as bank stocks gained 1.5% ahead of earnings and oil briefly eased on Trump's Russia Ukraine 'energy ceasefire' claim, which Russia did not confirm. Spain's bank heavy IBEX led with a 1.3% gain.
changes.for_you: No action. European banks are not on the dashboard. TTE is left out because the truce headline cut one way and the oil rebound the other.

changes.what: European stocks held up through the global chip selloff. The Stoxx 600 closed up 0.65% at 635.65 on Oct 12 and rose about 0.6% to a one week high early Oct 13, led by banks and energy, because Europe owns few AI chip giants. Disappointing LVMH results weighed on luxury. ASML reports later this week.
changes.for_you: No action. ASML is left out of both lists until it reports; memory makers are big buyers of its tools, so its outlook matters for LRCX and AMAT too.

changes.what: ASML, Europe's biggest tech company, reported Q3 sales of EUR 11.7 billion and raised its 2026 sales outlook to EUR 44 to 45 billion, the third raise this year. It said planned supply will not fully meet customer demand in 2027 and 2028. The Amsterdam shares were up about 1.75% to EUR 1,536 before the open.
changes.for_you: No action. ASML has no dashboard verdict (Not enough data, a currency mismatch), so it is not a buy zone call. It is a good sign for TSM before Thursday's report.

changes.what: Zelenskyy told the Financial Times that Ukraine will resume strikes on Russian refineries because Russia kept hitting Ukraine's grid during the three day energy truce; on Oct 15 Russia said a drone set the Ryazan refinery on fire. The US is separately weighing easing shadow fleet tanker sanctions to cut freight costs.
changes.for_you: No action. A failed truce keeps diesel and European energy costs high, which helps TTE and keeps the ECB hiking. STLA is left out of both lists because the effect on carmakers is indirect.

changes.what: Ericsson beat on Q3 sales (SEK 59.5 billion, 7% organic growth) and its ADR jumped 11.8% on Oct 15, while European chip stocks fell again: ASM International about 7% and Infineon about 5% (CNBC). AI hardware is under pressure in Europe too, but telecom networks are recovering.
changes.for_you: No action. ERIC has no dashboard verdict. ASML (1,657.44 ADR, up 0.5% on Oct 15) is rated 'Not enough data', so it is left out of both lists.

changes.what: Reuters reported on Oct 17 that Rosneft's Ryazan refinery, which supplies Moscow, halted its main crude unit (CDU-6) after Ukraine's Oct 15 drone strike (Kyiv Independent). A suspected Ukrainian drone also set fire to the Surgut condensate stabilization plant in western Siberia on Oct 16 (Moscow Times). Fewer working Russian units means less Russian diesel for export, which keeps European fuel costs high into winter.
changes.for_you: No action. TTE has no buy zone verdict. This keeps diesel and inflation pressure on Europe, which supports more ECB hikes at the Oct 29 meeting and helps European banks (SAN, ING) more than industrials.

changes.what: French bonds and stocks fell Oct 19 after a weekend of riots: the 10 year yield rose to about 4.84% to 4.89%, the gap over German bonds reached about 142 to 146 basis points, and the CAC 40 fell about 1% to 1.4% by midday, with Societe Generale and BNP Paribas down more than 2%. Parliament votes on 2027 budget revenues Oct 20 and Moody's reviews France Oct 23. Separately, Trump waived the Graham Act's new Russia tariffs and sanctions on Oct 16, which pushed Brent down about 2% Monday.
changes.for_you: No action. No dashboard name is French. SAN (13.30) and ING (33.45) had up/down volume under 0.75 on Friday, and French stress tends to spill into all euro banks, so do not buy them into Moody's. TTE is left out: cheaper oil and a weaker euro pull in opposite directions.

changes.what: France's National Assembly set the revenue vote on the 2027 budget for Nov 3 instead of Oct 20 (TokenPost, Oct 20), so Moody's reviews France's Aa3 negative rating on Oct 23 with no budget passed. The prime minister promised more curfews after the worst unrest in years, and the CAC 40 fell 0.38% to 7,838.49 with French 10 year yields near a 24 year high.
changes.for_you: No action. SAN and ING are left out of both lists: higher rates help their margins, French stress hurts European bank spreads. Wait until after Moody's on Friday. No dashboard name is French.

The gap over German bonds is near its widest since 2011. Moody's reviews France's Aa3 negative rating on Oct 23.
